translations.literal: At the time they wished to divide Jingzhou and establish Yingzhou, and debated where its seat should be.
translations.idiomatic: At the time they wished to divide Jingzhou and establish Yingzhou, and debated where its seat should be.

sentences.zh: 江夏王義恭以為宜在巴陵，尚之議曰：「夏口在荊、江之中，正對沔口，通接雍、梁，實為津要，由來舊鎮，根基不易。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, held that it should be at Baling. Shangzhi argued: "Xiakou lies between Jing and the Yangtze, directly facing the mouth of the Han, connecting with Yong and Liang—it is truly a strategic crossing. It has long been an old garrison and its foundations are not easily changed.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, held that it should be at Baling. Shangzhi argued: "Xiakou lies between Jing and the Yangtze, directly facing the mouth of the Han, connecting with Yong and Liang—it is truly a strategic crossing. It has long been an old garrison and its foundations are not easily changed.

sentences.zh: 今分取江夏、武陵、天門、竟陵、隨五郡為一州，鎮在夏口，既有見城，浦大容舫。

translations.literal: Now take Jiangxia, Wuling, Tianmen, Jingling, and Sui—five commanderies—as one province, with the garrison at Xiakou. There is already an existing city, and the harbor is large enough to hold ships.
translations.idiomatic: Now take Jiangxia, Wuling, Tianmen, Jingling, and Sui—five commanderies—as one province, with the garrison at Xiakou. There is already an existing city, and the harbor is large enough to hold ships.

sentences.zh: 竟陵出道取荊州，雖水路，與去江夏不異，諸郡至夏口皆從流，並為利便。

translations.literal: From Jingling the route out to Jingzhou, though by water, differs little from going to Jiangxia; all commanderies reaching Xiakou follow the current, and all is convenient.
translations.idiomatic: From Jingling the route out to Jingzhou, though by water, differs little from going to Jiangxia; all commanderies reaching Xiakou follow the current, and all is convenient.

sentences.zh: 湘州所領十一郡，其巴陵邊帶長江，去夏口密邇，既分湘中，乃更成大，亦可割巴陵屬新州，於事為允。」

translations.literal: The eleven commanderies under Xiangzhou include Baling along the Yangtze, close to Xiakou. Since central Xiang has been divided, it has become even larger; Baling may also be cut off to belong to the new province, which in the affair is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: The eleven commanderies under Xiangzhou include Baling along the Yangtze, close to Xiakou. Since central Xiang has been divided, it has become even larger; Baling may also be cut off to belong to the new province, which would be fitting."

sentences.zh: 上從其議。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his view.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed his view.

sentences.zh: 荊、揚二州，戶口半天下，江左以來，揚州根本，委荊以閫外，至是並分，欲以削臣下之權，而荊、揚並因此虛耗。

translations.literal: Jing and Yang, the two provinces, held half the empire's registered households. Since the east of the Yangtze, Yangzhou was the root and Jing was entrusted with matters beyond the gate; now both were divided to cut down the power of subjects below, and Jing and Yang were both thereby drained and weakened.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Yang, the two provinces, held half the empire's registered households. Since the east of the Yangtze, Yangzhou was the root and Jing was entrusted with matters beyond the gate; now both were divided to cut down the power of subjects below, and Jing and Yang were both thereby drained and weakened.

sentences.zh: 尚之建言復合二州，上不許。

translations.literal: Shangzhi proposed reuniting the two provinces; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi proposed reuniting the two provinces; the emperor did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，以為左光祿、開府儀同三司，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming he was made Left Grand Master of the Palace with the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies, retaining his post as Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daming he was made Left Grand Master of the Palace with the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies, retaining his post as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 尚之在家常著鹿皮帽，及拜開府，天子臨軒，百僚陪位，沈慶之於殿廷戲之曰：「今日何不著鹿皮冠？」

translations.literal: At home Shangzhi often wore a deerskin cap. When he was invested with the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies, the Son of Heaven came to the hall and all officials attended in place. Shen Qingzhi jested in the court hall, "Why not wear your deerskin cap today?"
translations.idiomatic: At home Shangzhi often wore a deerskin cap. When he was invested with the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies, the Son of Heaven came to the hall and all officials attended. Shen Qingzhi jested in the court hall, "Why not wear your deerskin cap today?"

sentences.zh: 慶之累辭爵命，朝廷敦勸甚篤，尚之謂曰：「主上虛懷側席，詎宜固辭。」

translations.literal: Qingzhi repeatedly declined ennoblement; the court earnestly urged him with great sincerity. Shangzhi said to him, "The sovereign empties his mind and sits sidewise—how could you firmly decline?"
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi repeatedly declined ennoblement; the court earnestly urged him with great sincerity. Shangzhi said to him, "The sovereign empties his mind and sits sidewise—how could you firmly decline?"

sentences.zh: 慶之曰：「沈公不効何公，去而復還也。」

translations.literal: Qingzhi said, "Master Shen does not imitate Master He—going away and coming back again."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi said, "Master Shen does not imitate Master He—going away and coming back again."

sentences.zh: 尚之有愧色。

translations.literal: Shangzhi showed a look of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi showed a look of shame.

sentences.zh: 愛尚文義，老而不休，與太常顏延之論議往反，傳於世。

translations.literal: He loved and honored literary meaning and, old though he was, did not cease. With Yan Yanzhi, Minister of Ceremonies, he debated back and forth, and this was transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He loved literature and, old though he was, did not cease. With Yan Yanzhi, Minister of Ceremonies, he debated back and forth, and their exchanges were transmitted in the world.

sentences.zh: 立身簡約，車服率素，妻亡不娶，又無姬妾。

translations.literal: In personal conduct he was simple and restrained; carriages and dress were generally plain. When his wife died he did not remarry, nor did he keep concubines.
translations.idiomatic: In personal conduct he was simple and restrained; carriages and dress were generally plain. When his wife died he did not remarry, nor did he keep concubines.

sentences.zh: 秉衡當朝，畏遠權柄，親戚故舊，一無薦舉，既以致怨，亦以此見稱。

translations.literal: Holding the scales of office in the court, he feared and kept distant from power; among kin and old friends he made not a single recommendation. This both brought resentment and won him praise.
translations.idiomatic: Holding high office in the court, he feared and kept distant from power; among kin and old friends he made not a single recommendation. This both brought resentment and won him praise.

sentences.zh: 復以本官領中書令。

translations.literal: He again held his former office and concurrently served as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He again held his former office and concurrently served as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 四年，疾篤，詔遣侍中沈懷文、黃門侍郎王釗問疾。

translations.literal: In the fourth year his illness grew grave; an edict sent Palace Attendant Shen Huaiwen and Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate Wang Zhao to inquire after his health.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year his illness grew grave; an edict sent Palace Attendant Shen Huaiwen and Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate Wang Zhao to inquire after his health.

sentences.zh: 薨于位，時年七十九。

translations.literal: He died in office at the age of seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at the age of seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 追贈司空，侍中、中書令如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted Minister of Works, retaining his posts as Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat as before.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted Minister of Works, retaining his posts as Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 諡曰簡穆公。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Duke Jian Mu.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Duke Jian Mu.

sentences.zh: 子偃，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Yan has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 尚之弟悠之，義興太守，侍中，太常。

translations.literal: Shangzhi's younger brother Youzhi was Administrator of Yixing, Palace Attendant, and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi's younger brother Youzhi was Administrator of Yixing, Palace Attendant, and Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 與琅邪王微相善，悠之卒，微與偃書曰：「吾與義興，直恨相知之晚，每惟君子知我。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Wang Wei of Langye. When Youzhi died, Wei wrote to Yan: "I and the Administrator of Yixing only regret that we knew each other late; I always thought that a gentleman understood me.
translations.idiomatic: He was on good terms with Wang Wei of Langye. When Youzhi died, Wei wrote to Yan: "The Administrator of Yixing and I only regret that we knew each other late; I always thought that a gentleman understood me.

sentences.zh: 若夫嘉我小善，矜余不能，唯賢叔耳。」

translations.literal: As for praising my small good points and pitying my incapacities—only your worthy uncle did that."
translations.idiomatic: As for praising my small good points and pitying my incapacities—only your worthy uncle did that."

sentences.zh: 悠之弟愉之，新安太守。

translations.literal: Youzhi's younger brother Yuzhi was Administrator of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi's younger brother Yuzhi was Administrator of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 愉之弟翌之，都官尚書。

translations.literal: Yuzhi's younger brother Yizhi was Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhi's younger brother Yizhi was Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 悠之子顒之，尚太祖第四女臨海惠公主。

translations.literal: Youzhi's son Yongzhi married the fourth daughter of Emperor Taizu, the Princess Hui of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi's son Yongzhi married the fourth daughter of Emperor Taizu, the Princess Hui of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 太宗世，官至通直常侍。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Taizong he rose to Regular Attendant for Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: In the era of Emperor Taizong he rose to Regular Attendant for Direct Communication.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historian's appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Historian's Appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：江左以來，樹根本於揚越，任推轂於荊楚。

translations.literal: The historian says: Since the east of the Yangtze, the root has been planted in Yang and Yue, and the pushing of the chariot-wheel has been entrusted to Jing and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Since the east of the Yangtze, the root has been planted in Yang and Yue, and the pushing of the chariot-wheel has been entrusted to Jing and Chu.

sentences.zh: 揚土自廬、蠡以北，臨海而極大江；

translations.literal: The territory of Yang from Lu and Li northward borders the sea and reaches the great river;
translations.idiomatic: The territory of Yang from Lu and Li northward borders the sea and reaches the great river;

sentences.zh: 荊部則包括湘、沅，跨巫山而掩鄧塞。

translations.literal: the Jing region embraces Xiang and Yuan, spans Mount Wu, and covers the passes of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: the Jing region embraces Xiang and Yuan, spans Mount Wu, and covers the passes of Deng.

sentences.zh: 民戶境域，過半於天下。

translations.literal: Its registered households and territory were more than half of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Its registered households and territory were more than half of all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 晉世幼主在位，政歸輔臣，荊、揚司牧，事同二陝。

translations.literal: In the Jin age, when young lords held the throne, government returned to assisting ministers; the governors of Jing and Yang were matters like the two Shans.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jin age, when young lords held the throne, government returned to assisting ministers; the governors of Jing and Yang were matters like the two Shans.

sentences.zh: 宋室受命，權不能移，二州之重，咸歸密戚。

translations.literal: When the Song house received the Mandate, power could not be shifted; the weight of the two provinces all returned to close kin.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song house received the Mandate, power could not be shifted; the weight of the two provinces all returned to close kin.

sentences.zh: 是以義宣藉西楚強富，因十載之基，嫌隙既樹，遂規問鼎。

translations.literal: Thus Yixuan relied on the strength and wealth of western Chu, built on a foundation of ten years; once rancor was planted, he then plotted to seize the tripod.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Yixuan relied on the strength and wealth of western Chu, built on a foundation of ten years; once rancor was planted, he then plotted to seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 而建郢分揚，矯枉過直，藩城既剖，盜實人單，閫外之寄，於斯而盡。

translations.literal: Yet in establishing Ying and dividing Yang, straightening the bent went too far. Once the barrier cities were cut apart, the substance of banditry was thinned and men were few; the trust placed beyond the gate ended at this point.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in establishing Ying and dividing Yang, straightening the bent went too far. Once the barrier cities were cut apart, the substance of rebellion was thinned and men were few; the trust placed beyond the gate ended at this point.

sentences.zh: 若長君南面，威刑自出，至親在外，事不患強。

translations.literal: If a mature ruler faces south, authority and punishments issue from himself, and the closest kin are outside, the matter need not fear strength.
translations.idiomatic: If a mature ruler faces south, authority and punishments issue from himself, and the closest kin are outside, the matter need not fear strength.

sentences.zh: 若運經盛衰，時艱主弱，雖近臣懷禍，止有外憚，呂宗不競，實由齊、楚，興喪之源，於斯尤著。

translations.literal: If fortune passes through rise and decline, the times are hard and the ruler weak, though near ministers harbor malice they have only outward fear. The Lü clan did not contend—truly because of Qi and Chu; the source of rise and fall is especially clear here.
translations.idiomatic: If fortune passes through rise and decline, the times are hard and the ruler weak, though near ministers harbor malice they have only outward fear. The Lü clan did not contend—truly because of Qi and Chu; the source of rise and fall is especially clear here.

sentences.zh: 尚之言并合，可謂識治也矣。

translations.literal: Shangzhi's words on reuniting them may be called understanding of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi's words on reuniting them may be called understanding of governance.
